title: Special Products and Factorization

instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Every answer shows the working. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: (x + 8)(x − 10) is equal to —
The factors of 3x² − x − 4 are —
questions.work:
Product ac = 3 × (−4) = −12; we need two numbers with product −12 and sum −1: they are −4 and 3.
3x² − x − 4 = 3x² − 4x + 3x − 4
= x(3x − 4) + 1(3x − 4) = (3x − 4)(x + 1).

questions.q: 4x² − 9y² is equal to —
questions.work:
4x² − 9y² = (2x)² − (3y)², a difference of two squares.
a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), so 4x² − 9y² = (2x + 3y)(2x − 3y).

questions.q: 1 + x + xy + x²y is equal to —
questions.work:
Group the terms: (1 + x) + (xy + x²y)
= (1 + x) + xy(1 + x)
= (1 + x)(1 + xy).

questions.q: x² − 5x + 6 is equal to —
questions.work:
Two numbers with product +6 and sum −5 are −3 and −2.
So x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 3)(x − 2).
Check: (x − 3)(x − 2) = x² − 2x − 3x + 6 = x² − 5x + 6.

questions.q: The HCF of 3³ × 5 and 3² × 5² is —
questions.work:
HCF takes each common prime factor with its lowest power.
Power of 3: lower of 3 and 2 → 3²; power of 5: lower of 1 and 2 → 5¹.
HCF = 3² × 5 = 9 × 5 = 45.

questions.q: If a/b + b/a = 1 (a, b ≠ 0), then a³ + b³ is —
questions.work:
a/b + b/a = 1 ⇒ (a² + b²)/ab = 1 ⇒ a² + b² = ab ⇒ a² − ab + b² = 0.
a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) = (a + b) × 0 = 0.

questions.q: The HCF of two numbers is 3 and their LCM is 21. If one number is 7, the other is —
questions.work:
Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 3 × 21 = 63.
Other number = 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

questions.q: If 25x² − 2xy + y²/25 = (5x + ky)², then k is —
questions.work:
(5x + ky)² = 25x² + 10kxy + k²y².
Compare the xy terms: 10k = −2 ⇒ k = −1/5.
Check: k² = 1/25, which matches y²/25.

questions.q: The LCM of 4x²y³ and x³y² (x, y prime) is —
questions.work:
Numbers: LCM(4, 1) = 4.
x: higher power of x² and x³ is x³; y: higher power of y³ and y² is y³.
LCM = 4x³y³.

questions.q: x³ + 216 factorizes as —
questions.work:
216 = 6³, so x³ + 216 = x³ + 6³.
Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) with a = x, b = 6:
x³ + 216 = (x + 6)(x² − 6x + 36).

questions.q: (2x² + 5)² − (2x² − 5)² is equal to —

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) (x² + 3)² + (x² − 3)² = ________. (ii) (a − 5b)³ = ________.
questions.answer:
(i) Use (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) with a = x², b = 3:
2(x⁴ + 9) = 2x⁴ + 18.
(ii) Use (x − y)³ = x³ − 3x²y + 3xy² − y³ with x = a, y = 5b:
a³ − 3a²(5b) + 3a(5b)² − (5b)³ = a³ − 15a²b + 75ab² − 125b³.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The HCF of x³ − y³ and x² − y² is ________. (ii) Their LCM is ________.
questions.answer:
x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²) and x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y).
(i) The only common factor is (x − y), so HCF = x − y.
(ii) LCM = (x − y)(x + y)(x² + xy + y²) = (x + y)(x³ − y³).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The HCF of x³ + 1 and x² − 1 is ________. (ii) (2x² + 5)² − (2x² − 5)² = ________.
questions.answer:
(i) x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1) and x² − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1); common factor x + 1, so HCF = x + 1.
(ii) (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab = 4 × 2x² × 5 = 40x².

(i) 64a³ + 27b³ = (4a)³ + (3b)³ = (4a + 3b)(16a² − 12ab + 9b²), using a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
(ii) Same denominator, so add the numerators: (x² + 1 + x² − 1)/(x − 2) = 2x²/(x − 2).

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) (x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy. (ii) The HCF of 6x²y and 9xy² is 3x²y².
questions.answer:
(i) True: (x² + 2xy + y²) − (x² − 2xy + y²) = 4xy.
(ii) False: HCF of 6 and 9 is 3; lowest powers are x¹ and y¹, so HCF = 3xy.

questions.q: Match: (i) a³ − b³ (ii) a² − b² — (A) (a − b)(a + b) (B) (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) (C) (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)
questions.answer:
(i) a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) → (B).
(ii) a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) → (A).

sections.title: Case study: read the information and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The area of the whole garden is —
The area of the flower bed is —
The area of the grass is —
The volume of one box is —
If x = 10, the area of the grass is —

sections.passage: A school garden is a square of side (x + 5) m. A square flower bed of side (x − 5) m is made in one corner and the rest is grass. The gardener also stacks cube-shaped boxes of side (x + 1) m.

questions.q: Find the LCM of P(x) = x³ + 2x² − 3x and Q(x) = 2x³ + 5x² − 3x.
questions.answer:
P(x) = x(x² + 2x − 3) = x(x + 3)(x − 1).
Q(x) = x(2x² + 5x − 3) = x(2x² + 6x − x − 3) = x(2x − 1)(x + 3).
LCM = every factor with its highest power = x(x + 3)(x − 1)(2x − 1).

or.answer:
Square both sides: (x + 1/x)² = 4.
x² + 2 × x × (1/x) + 1/x² = 4 ⇒ x² + 2 + 1/x² = 4.
So x² + 1/x² = 4 − 2 = 2.

questions.q: Simplify (3x + 4y)² + (3x − 4y)².
If a + 1/a = 2, find a³ + 1/a³.
Find the HCF of x² − 4 and x² + 4x + 4.
questions.answer:
x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2).
x² + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)².
Common factor with the lowest power: (x + 2). HCF = x + 2.
questions.note: The April 2026 paper printed the second polynomial as x² + 4x + 8, which has no factor in common with x² − 4; x² + 4x + 4 is the intended form.

questions.answer:
Let a = 1.37, b = 0.37. The expression is (a³ − b³)/(a² + ab + b²).
Since a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), it equals a − b = 1.37 − 0.37 = 1.

questions.q: Factorise x² − 5x + 25/4.
Factorise a⁶ − 64b⁶.
questions.answer:
a⁶ − 64b⁶ = (a³)² − (8b³)² = (a³ − 8b³)(a³ + 8b³).
a³ − 8b³ = a³ − (2b)³ = (a − 2b)(a² + 2ab + 4b²).
a³ + 8b³ = a³ + (2b)³ = (a + 2b)(a² − 2ab + 4b²).
So a⁶ − 64b⁶ = (a − 2b)(a + 2b)(a² + 2ab + 4b²)(a² − 2ab + 4b²).

or.answer:
Factorise: a² − 1 = (a − 1)(a + 1); a² − 25 = (a − 5)(a + 5); a² − 4a − 5 = (a − 5)(a + 1); a² + 4a − 5 = (a + 5)(a − 1).
Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal:
[(a − 1)(a + 1)]/[(a − 5)(a + 5)] × [(a + 5)(a − 1)]/[(a − 5)(a + 1)].
Cancel (a + 1) and (a + 5): (a − 1)²/(a − 5)².

questions.q: If x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 119, find x − 1/x.
questions.answer:
x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2 ⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 121 ⇒ x² + 1/x² = 11 (it is positive).
(x − 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² − 2 = 11 − 2 = 9.
So x − 1/x = ±3.

questions.q: If x² + 1/x² = 7 (x > 0), find x³ + 1/x³.
Simplify (x² − x − 6)/(x² + 4x − 5) ÷ (x² − 4x + 3)/(x² + 6x + 5).
Simplify into the lowest form: (x² + x + 1)/(x² − 9) ÷ (x³ − 1)/(x² − 4x + 3).
If x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 34 (x > 0), find (i) x² + 1/x² (ii) x − 1/x (iii) x + 1/x.
questions.answer:
(i) (x² + 1/x²)² = x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 = 34 + 2 = 36, so x² + 1/x² = 6.
(ii) (x − 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² − 2 = 6 − 2 = 4, so x − 1/x = ±2.
(iii) (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2 = 6 + 2 = 8, so x + 1/x = 2√2 (positive because x > 0).
questions.note: April 2019 (4 marks) asked only for x − 1/x.

questions.q: Find the HCF and LCM of x² − 9, x² + 6x + 9 and x² + x − 6. Verify that HCF × LCM is not equal to the product of the three polynomials.
questions.answer:
x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)².
x² + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2).
HCF = common factor with lowest power = (x + 3).
LCM = all factors with highest powers = (x + 3)²(x − 3)(x − 2).
HCF × LCM = (x + 3)³(x − 3)(x − 2), but the product of the three is (x + 3)⁴(x − 3)(x − 2). They are not equal — the rule HCF × LCM = product holds only for two polynomials.
